title: Local isomorphisms under normalized stratum restriction
statement: Let i:S to X be an immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme], A a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and I an ideal. Let F be any algebraic inverse-image data for the normalized geometric inverse image along i [lem-sfb-adic-stratum-completion-unit]. Let U be an object of S_proet, and K,L arbitrary unbounded derived objects over adicLisseCompletedRing X I [def-sfb-adic-stratified-perfect-data]. If their sfbLocalRestriction at i,U are isomorphic, then completedPull F followed by the normalized slice completedPull at AsSmall.up(U), applied to their normalized objects [lem-sfb-completion-normalization], are isomorphic. No completeness, covering, stratification, perfectness, or Noetherianity of X or S is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11 reverse implication, gluing the completeness sentence on finite strata; Lemma 6.5.8(1) and Remark 6.5.10

proof.text: For the immersion and slice, inverse image preserves countable inverse limits, so both completed coefficient maps are invertible. Normalize the source by the canonical coefficient isomorphism. The ordinary immersion comparison constructs an appropriate target coefficient isomorphism. The ordinary slice comparison supplies an exact additive functor G from the original slice modules and the natural isomorphism of the composed ordinary module functors.

The module pulls along these invertible coefficient maps are exact. Their left-derived comparison is invertible on every complex. Cancel the fully faithful precomposition with the quasi-isomorphism localization to identify each completedPull with the exact induced derived functor. Compose the ordinary comparison, the derived composition isomorphisms, and the representative comparison for normalization and slice restriction. For each M this gives an isomorphism from its normalized completed restriction to G derived applied to its original local restriction.

Apply G derived to the given isomorphism and compose with the comparison for K and the inverse comparison for L. The construction uses no points or nonempty covers, so empty sites and zero coefficient rings are included.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 6.6.11 reverse implication; Y3 ordinary immersion/slice comparison followed by exact derived functoriality and localization representative isomorphisms.

theorem sfbNormalizedLocalRestriction_iso
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (i : S ⟶ X) [IsImmersion i]
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (I : Ideal A)
    (F : ConstantCompletion.InverseImageData (SfbAdicRestriction.inverse i))
    (U : S.ProEt)
    (K L : DerivedCategory (proEtaleRingModules X (adicLisseCompletedRing X I)))
    (h : Nonempty (sfbLocalRestriction i (adicLisseCompletedRing X I) U K ≅
      sfbLocalRestriction i (adicLisseCompletedRing X I) U L)) :
    Nonempty
      ((SfbAdicRestriction.completedPull F (SfbAdicRestriction.direct i)
          (SfbAdicRestriction.adjunction i) A I ⋙
        SfbAdicRestriction.completedPull
          (SfbAdicRestriction.sliceAlgebra (proEtaleModelTopology S) (AsSmall.up.obj U))
          (SfbAdicRestriction.sliceDirect (proEtaleModelTopology S) (AsSmall.up.obj U))
          (SfbAdicRestriction.sliceAdjunction (proEtaleModelTopology S) (AsSmall.up.obj U))
          A I).obj (SfbCompletionNormalization.object X I K) ≅
        (SfbAdicRestriction.completedPull F (SfbAdicRestriction.direct i)
          (SfbAdicRestriction.adjunction i) A I ⋙
        SfbAdicRestriction.completedPull
          (SfbAdicRestriction.sliceAlgebra (proEtaleModelTopology S) (AsSmall.up.obj U))
          (SfbAdicRestriction.sliceDirect (proEtaleModelTopology S) (AsSmall.up.obj U))
          (SfbAdicRestriction.sliceAdjunction (proEtaleModelTopology S) (AsSmall.up.obj U))
          A I).obj (SfbCompletionNormalization.object X I L))
